subject: Indemnity coordination: MSA / Order Form redline & escalation runbook
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@procurement.novahealth.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Huang <claire@novahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - indemnity items

David —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Procurement leadership asked I get ahead of a couple of stickier indemnity points before legal redlines land:

- Customer asks: carve out liability for third-party patent claims tied to data we upload to the model; full defense for downstream claims related to NovaHealth-branded outputs.
- They pushed back on our "right to defend" language and want joint-control or customer control with reimbursement.
- Escrow / holdback: they want an escrow mechanism if dispute > $5M.

Can Redwood provide a short tactical plan for negotiation sequencing and who on your side will own evidence triage / engineer engagement if a claim arises? We need this for our legal procurement packet.

Also attaching the procurement checklist (see attachment in their system). Appreciate a short note by EOD Monday.

—Raj
Procurement, NovaHealth

[Attachment referenced: Nova_Procurement_Checklist.pdf]

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@procurement.novahealth.com>, Claire Huang <claire@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - indemnity items

Raj / Claire —

Thanks — here is a concise tack we propose so procurement/legal can slot it into the packet. High-level sequencing and owners below. Will follow with redline doc and a short evidence-handling runbook.

1) Narrow scope by trigger and product:
   - We accept customer claims for output that directly reproduces a third-party work ("clear infringement") when the customer provides the content used as the prompt/material.
   - We push back on broad downstream indemnity for general model outputs — propose a carveout for "customer-modified outputs and integrations".
2) Defense control compromise:
   - Offer joint defense with customer right to lead technical discovery for claims about customer prompts/data.
   - If customer insists on control, offer customer control limited to the specific claim and with Redwood reserved rights to appoint counsel for technical matters.
3) Escrow / monetary mechanism:
   - We can accept an escrow trigger tied to final judgement or settlement above an agreed threshold (propose $10M; willing to discuss $5M with insurance backstop).
4) Evidence / engineering support:
   - Owner: Ben Carter (legal + ops liaison) will own evidence intake and initial triage. Engineering lead: Grace O'Connor will own log pulls and prompt/eval reproduction.
   - We will require a 10-business-day window for evidence handoff and a formal request template (samples attached).

Next steps (this week):
- Kimberly will push a targeted redline (MSA + Order Form) that implements the compromise language above and includes explicit evidence request template.
- I'll send the operational runbook (attachment) for procurement to review and flag any timing conflicts.

If that sequencing looks OK, propose a short joint call on Thursday to resolve the escrow threshold and defense control sentence.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced: Redwood_indemnity_tactical_plan.pdf]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: internal: proposed redlines and evidence template (draft)

Team —

Draft redlines attached (Nova_MSARedlines_v3.docx). Key changes called out:

- Trigger language tightened: indemnity only when customer provides the allegedly infringing material as input, or where output is a verbatim reproduction of a third party's copyrighted work.
- Defense control: proposed joint-defense paragraph with a technical carve-in for Redwood to appoint counsel on technical strategy; customer can lead financial settlement decisions but must consult.
- Escrow: added compromise language that accepts an escrow holdback for liabilities > $10M with an alternative to require proof of insurance coverage.
- Evidence template: 7 fields (claim id, sample prompt, sample output, timestamps, user-id hash, suggested reproduction steps, requested artifacts). We are strict on PII redaction and will require a court order for redaction exceptions.

Please review and add inline comments in the doc. Ben — I'll need you to prep the short engineer engagement SLA (10 business days for first triage, contact matrix for 24/7 escalations). Grace — will you confirm the logs we can provide and typical timelines?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Nova_MSARedlines_v3.docx, Indemnity_escrow_matrix.xlsx]

To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@procurement.novahealth.com>, Claire Huang <claire@novahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - indemnity items

Raj / Claire —

Quick update and delivery of the items we discussed. Attached: targeted MSA + Order Form redlines and a short evidence/ops runbook. Summary below to make the packet easy for your legal team:

- Scope: Redwood proposes indemnity for third-party IP claims only when the claim arises from
  (a) customer-supplied input material that directly caused the alleged infringement, or
  (b) outputs that are verbatim reproductions of a third party work. We decline broad downstream indemnity for general model outputs.
- Defense control: joint defense with customer control over settlement; Redwood reserved right to appoint technical counsel for code/model/discovery.
- Escrow: we proposed a $10M threshold. If Nova insists on $5M, Redwood asks for an insurance backstop and a defined settlement approval ladder (exec signoff + escrow draw process).
- Ops: Ben will be the evidence intake owner; Grace will run reproducibility checks. We included an evidence template and an SLA: 10-business-day triage for initial artifacts, 24/7 contact for critical escalations.

If this aligns with what procurement needs, would you like us to prep a redline exchange with a tracked DocuSign-ready packet or schedule a 30-minute call Thurs at 10am PT to walk through the escrow threshold?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best regards,
David Kim
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: Nova_MSARedlines_v3.docx; Indemnity_escrow_matrix.xlsx]
